content.section: 5.2. Acute coronary syndrome managed with invasive strategy
content.overview: Invasive management strategies are time sensitive. Patients with high suspicion of ongoing acute coronary artery occlusion (persistent ST-segment elevation or equivalents) or very high-risk NSTE-ACS should receive emergency angiography as soon as possible. High-risk NSTE-ACS patients (e.g. ruled in as NSTEMI by ESC algorithms, dynamic ST-segment/T wave changes, transient ST elevation, or GRACE risk score >140) should be considered for an early invasive strategy (angiography within 24 h).

primary_percutaneous_coronary_interventi.preferred_strategy: PPCI (immediate angiography and PCI as needed) is the preferred reperfusion strategy for patients with a working diagnosis of STEMI, provided it can be performed in a timely manner.
primary_percutaneous_coronary_interventi.timing_threshold: Within 120 minutes of the ECG-based diagnosis is the recommended absolute time limit for PPCI to be preferred over fibrinolysis.
primary_percutaneous_coronary_interventi.evidence_summary: Randomized controlled trials show PPCI is superior to fibrinolysis in reducing mortality, non-fatal reinfarction and stroke if delay to treatment is similar.

treatment_delay_considerations.absolute_time_definition: An absolute time of 120 minutes from STEMI diagnosis to PCI-mediated reperfusion is used for simplicity to define when PPCI should be preferred.
treatment_delay_considerations.relative_delay_notes: Given recommended intervals (including 10 min to bolus of fibrinolytics), the 120 min absolute time corresponds to a relative PCI-related delay range identified in older studies and registries.

fibrinolysis_and_rescue_PCI.when_to_initiate_fibrinolysis: If PPCI is not an immediate option, fibrinolysis should be initiated expediently as part of a pharmaco-invasive strategy provided patient presented within 12 h of symptom onset.
fibrinolysis_and_rescue_PCI.rescue_PCI_indications: Rescue PCI is indicated if fibrinolysis fails (ST-segment resolution <50% within 60–90 min of fibrinolytic administration) or in the presence of haemodynamic/electrical instability, worsening ischaemia, or persistent chest pain.
fibrinolysis_and_rescue_PCI.post_successful_fibrinolysis: Patients with successful fibrinolysis should undergo early invasive angiography (within approximately 2–24 h from the time of the lytic bolus injection).

transfer_guidance_for_non_PCI_centres.immediate_transfer: Patients with working diagnosis of STEMI who present to a non-PCI centre should be immediately transferred to a PCI-capable centre for timely PPCI.
transfer_guidance_for_non_PCI_centres.if_PPCI_not_feasible: If PPCI cannot be achieved within 120 minutes, immediate fibrinolysis should be given followed by transfer to a PCI centre without waiting for signs of reperfusion.

content.special_notes: For patients presenting after 12 h from symptom onset, a PPCI strategy is preferred over fibrinolysis in all cases.
references_cited_on_page: Multiple citation numbers appear (e.g., 52, 179, 176, 180a, 184, 184, 185, 186) indicating supporting studies/registry data
